payload.claim: [host-filed criterion probe] tests/test_session.py::test_a_rebut_session_that_dies_is_never_read_as_a_pool_cut stayed green with the criterion's own edit applied to saffron/cell/session.py. The claim was "A REBUT session that fails without the budget signal is never a pool cut, whatever it spent. That covers a death with no result event, an `api_error` result, a turn ceiling and a failure carrying no attempt. The task ends where `run_rebut` put it. The budget signal `cut_off_at_budget_cap` reads is a cut at any spend, even after a death in the same REBUT stage. A refusal of a call the stage's pool cannot cover is a cut too, unless a death without the signal brought that stage's spend to its limit. Each cut still ends `EXHAUSTED` with its stage's line. The witness drives one REBUT per row through `_rebut_capped` and reads the outcome's state, the `TaskOutcome` event, the queued state and the last REBUT line. In each of the three stages, a death with no result event at its pool, past it and under it ends `REBUTTAL_UNJUDGED`. So do an `api_error` result and a turn ceiling past the pool. The first two stages name the session's own error, and the verdict stage says a lens produced no verdict. No such line says REBUT ran out, and `rebut_result` stays. A rebuttal turn that raises with no attempt ends the same way. A session that succeeds and spends the extraction's pool to the cent, then claims a fix it did not commit, ends `REBUTTAL_UNJUDGED` too. In each stage the budget signal under the pool and at it ends `EXHAUSTED` with the stage's line. One rebuttal-stage row carries `terminal_reason` alone and the other `subtype` alone, and the extraction stage swaps them. The pool refusing the extraction's re-prompt, and refusing a second verdict, each ends `EXHAUSTED` with the stage's line. Each row with two blocker lenses refuses the second. After a first verdict that dies at the pool, it ends `REBUTTAL_UNJUDGED`. After one that ends on the budget signal, it ends `EXHAUSTED`. An extraction that dies at its pool, then a first verdict that spends the verdicts' pool, still ends `EXHAUSTED` on the refused second verdict. Two rows start the verdicts with a death under the verdicts' pool. In one a second lens spends the rest and a third is refused. In the other the second ends on the budget signal. Each ends `EXHAUSTED` with the verdict line. The witness checks every row before it asserts once, on the list of rows that disagreed.", and the whole `tests` gate stayed green under the edit too.
